summary:
MISSION CONTROL: BEYOND THE BLUEPRINT is an interactive, web-based space engineering strategy and simulation game set in the year 2042. It puts players in the role of Chief Mission Designers, challenging them to design spacecraft, select components, manage limited resources, plan missions, and respond to unexpected emergencies.

The game addresses the challenge by transforming space exploration and spacecraft engineering concepts into an engaging, hands-on learning experience. Through six gameplay stages, players make critical engineering decisions involving power, propulsion, communication, fuel, and scientific instruments. Its standout feature, the Mission Crisis Engine, connects players' initial design choices to the challenges they encounter during missions, demonstrating how preparation and engineering decisions influence mission outcomes.

Featuring missions such as Lunar Shadows, our project encourages critical thinking, problem-solving, resource management, and scientific curiosity. It is important because it makes complex space engineering concepts more accessible and allows people to experience the decision-making involved in real-world space exploration.
details:
Project Details: MISSION CONTROL: BEYOND THE BLUEPRINT

MISSION CONTROL: BEYOND THE BLUEPRINT is an interactive, web-based space engineering strategy and simulation game that allows players to experience the responsibilities of designing and managing a spacecraft mission.

How it works: Set in the fictional year 2042, the game places players in the role of Chief Mission Designers. Players progress through six stages: Mission Briefing, Spacecraft Design, Mission Planning, Launch and Simulation, Mission Crisis, and Mission Results. They select spacecraft components such as propulsion systems, power supplies, communication equipment, fuel systems, scientific instruments, and protective systems. Each component has different costs, mass, power requirements, and reliability levels. Players must balance their budget and available resources while preparing their spacecraft for missions.

The game introduces unexpected challenges such as solar storms, fuel leaks, communication failures, battery malfunctions, and thermal emergencies. Its signature feature, the Mission Crisis Engine, connects the player's earlier engineering decisions to how their spacecraft responds to these emergencies. This means that two players facing the same crisis can experience different outcomes depending on how they designed their spacecraft.

Benefits and intended impact: The project makes space engineering concepts more engaging and accessible. It encourages critical thinking, problem-solving, decision-making, risk assessment, resource management, and scientific curiosity. Our aim is to inspire learners to explore engineering and understand the importance of careful planning in space exploration.

Development tools and technologies: The project uses HTML5, CSS3, Bootstrap 5, JavaScript (ES6), Three.js, and Chart.js, alongside NASA data and APIs where applicable. GitHub supports version control and collaboration, while platforms such as Vercel or Netlify support web deployment. It is designed to run through a web browser without requiring specialized hardware.

Creativity and innovation: Our creativity lies in combining spacecraft engineering with interactive gameplay. Rather than simply presenting information about space, we allow players to make engineering decisions and experience their consequences. The Mission Crisis Engine makes the experience more dynamic by ensuring that design choices matter beyond the initial spacecraft-building stage.

Factors considered: Our team considered scientific relevance, realistic engineering trade-offs, limited resources, mission objectives, usability, accessibility, gameplay balance, and the educational value of the experience. We also considered different exploration environments, including the Moon, Mars, Europa, and deep space, to demonstrate the variety of challenges involved in space exploration.
